title: Constant-extension Weil hearts, cyclic sheets and residue-degree Frobenius powers
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ as in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $m\ge1$, $k_m=\mathbf F_{q^m}\subset k$, $X_{0,m}=X_0\times_{k_0}k_m$, and $g_m:X_{0,m}\to X_0$ the projection. All coefficient categories and constructible Weil sheaves are those of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] and [def-weil-constructible-heart].

(a) For any constructible Weil sheaf $\mathcal F=(M,\theta)$ on $X_0$, its restriction to the $k_m$-scheme $X_{0,m}$ has underlying object $M$ on $X$ and Weil map
$$\theta^{[m]}=\theta\circ Lg_X^*\theta\circ\cdots\circ L(g_X^{m-1})^*\theta,$$
where $g_X$ is geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. This restriction is exact. If $z\in X_{0,m}$ is closed with image $x\in X_0$ and $f=[\kappa(z):\kappa(x)]$, its local operator, using exactly the iterated point transports of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], is conjugate to $F_x^f$, and $q_z=q_x^f$. Equivalently, if $d=[\kappa(x):k_0]$, then $f=m/\gcd(d,m)$. These assertions hold for constructible sheaves, without a lissity or semisimplicity hypothesis.

(b) Write $W_{k_m}(X_{0,m})$ for its constructible Weil heart as a $k_m$-scheme and $W_{k_0}(X_{0,m})$ for its constructible Weil heart when the same scheme is viewed over $k_0$. The geometric scheme in the second category is $X_{0,m}\times_{k_0}k$, a disjoint union of $m$ sheets isomorphic to $X$, cyclically permuted by geometric $q$-Frobenius. Restriction to the sheet for the inclusion $k_m\subset k$, together with the return isomorphism around this cycle, gives an exact equivalence
$$W_{k_0}(X_{0,m})\simeq W_{k_m}(X_{0,m}).$$
Its inverse places the successive Frobenius translates on the sheets and uses the given $q^m$-Weil map for the return. It identifies subobjects, quotients and finite filtrations. At a closed point $z$ of $X_{0,m}$ the two interpretations have the same local operator up to conjugacy and the same absolute residue size $\#\kappa(z)$. Thus corresponding quotients are punctually pure of the same weight, and finite mixed filtrations with any specified weight bound correspond. Applied to the object in (a), the inverse gives precisely the $k_0$-Weil pullback $g_m^*\mathcal F$ on this disjoint geometric scheme, before applying $g_{m,*}$.

proof.text: For constantExtensionCyclicSheets, take the existing geometric package of [lem-zl-constant-extension-sheet-geometry]. Each cyclic map factors as its coordinate isomorphism followed by its clopen open inclusion, hence is an open and closed immersion. The ranges equal the package opens; their pairwise disjointness and supremum equal to top give the coproduct by Scheme.nonempty_isColimit_cofanMk_of. Apply the package return_map at i=m-1, identify positive powers with automorphism powers, and simplify the zeroth cyclic sheet to obtain the required mth-power return equation. The argument applies also to the empty scheme and m=1.

source.place: Paragraph after (1.1.10), p.152; clopen cyclic geometric sheets.

proof.text: Obtain the sheet-return functor S with its local conjugacy, purity and mixedness assertions from lem-zl-constant-extension-return-local-operators. Obtain a functor T satisfying the same normalized sheet specification and T.IsEquivalence from lem-zl-sheet-return-exact-functor. Compose their carrier comparisons; the specified return equations make this a natural Weil isomorphism T≅S. Transfer IsEquivalence to S and take e=S.asEquivalence. Equivalences preserve all finite limits and colimits.

Obtain the exact restriction R₀ and normalized G≅g_m^* from lem-zl-constant-extension-pullback-return-residue. The zeroth normalization comparison, composed with the sheet-specification comparison of S, lifts to a natural Weil isomorphism G⋙S≅R₀: its Weil equation is exactly the normalization return equation followed by the sheet-specification equation. Whisker G≅g_m^* to obtain g_m^*⋙S≅R₀. Transfer the restriction specification and finite-limit/colimit preservation along this isomorphism. The unit of e identifies (g_m^*⋙e.functor)⋙e.inverse with g_m^*. For any Weil object, its successive invertible sheet transitions identify every sheet carrier with its zeroth sheet carrier; compose with the sheet specification and the counit of e to prove the inverse-sheet assertion.

Use the residue compositum theorem for the residue-degree and cardinality formulas. Apply lem-zl-constant-extension-restriction-local-conjugacy to S with its sheet specification for the local-power assertion of restriction. Use the local-operator and weight equivalences of S obtained in the second step for the two-interpretation local conjugacy and the punctual-purity/mixedness clauses. The same arguments include m=1, empty schemes and zero stalks.

proof_origin.place: (1.1.7)--(1.1.10), pp.150--152; exact sheet return and its weight comparison, normalized pullback return, and residue-power comparison assembled by natural Weil isomorphisms.
